headline: SOSMA Renewal Cycles: Section 4(11) Requires 5-Year Parliamentary Review of Section 4(5) Detention
context: SOSMA Section 4(11) requires Parliament to extend or let lapse the 28-day pre-charge detention authority in Section 4(5) every five years. The July 2022 renewal passed 111-88. Civil society has called for substantive reform alongside renewal.

changes.summary: Correction: Removed unverified details of a 2024 renewal (a 45-minute debate, 23 MPs taking part, a 15,000-signature petition). Added Suaram's arrest data.
Correction: Fixed the section citation: section 4(11) sets the five-year review of the section 4(5) detention power. Added the July 2022 renewal vote of 111 to 88.

Correction: 6,892 is the Home Minister's count of SOSMA detentions from 2012 to 2025, which Suaram cited; earlier editions called it Suaram's arrest figure. A parliamentary select committee called in December 2025 for the 28-day period to be reviewed.

cards.big: SOSMA Section 4(11) requires Parliament to extend or let lapse the 28-day pre-charge detention authority every five years.
cards.sub: The July 2022 Dewan Rakyat renewal passed 111 in favour, 88 against, 21 absent, on the day it was moved. The 2012 Bill's debate ran across two sitting days.

cards.big: SOSMA Section 4(11) sets the five-year review trigger for the Section 4(5) Superintendent-or-above detention power.
cards.sub: The 2022 renewal was a motion put to a vote. Separately, in December 2025, a parliamentary select committee urged a review of the 28-day period.

cards.big: The Home Minister counted 6,892 SOSMA detentions from 2012 to 2025. Suaram reports 20-28% of SOSMA detainees are released without charge.
cards.sub: The count did not exist at the 2022 renewal vote: it came in a March 2026 written reply, which Suaram cited in April 2026.

cards.big: Civil-society organisations (Bar Council, Suaram, Lawyers for Liberty) have publicly urged MPs to reject the renewal or repeal SOSMA.
cards.sub: Renewal procedure does not require parliamentary acknowledgement of public submissions, and those submissions are not part of the formal debate record.

cards.big: The renewal mechanism extends an investigative-detention authority. It is not designed to revisit whether the authority should still exist.
Like renewing a licence with a tick-box form: the paperwork advances, the underlying decision is never re-examined.
cards.sub: Renewal procedure is not the same as substantive review.

cards.big: A law permitting 28-day pre-charge detention warrants substantive review at every renewal, anchored on official detention counts and Suaram's release-without-charge data.
